title: Probe design and telemetry scenarios for rollbacks
body:
Purpose
- Capture a concise, actionable approach to designing telemetry probes and tracing scenarios that are specifically targeted at informing safe rollbacks and automatic fallback decisions for inference services.
- Focus: production token-serving paths, KV cache behavior, batching, and model-variant fallbacks.

High-level goals
- Provide observability signals that let platform automation decide: continue rollout, pause, rollback, or route to fallback model.
- Keep trace capture and metric cardinality within cost budget (probe fidelity budget).
- Ensure fast investigation surface for SRE/SEs (1–3 minute mean time to actionable insight).

Scope / non-goals
- In-scope: hosted inference endpoints, Dedicated pools, model routing decisions, rollout canaries.
- Out-of-scope: full upstream model training telemetry, customer application layer beyond request meta.

Definitions (for this doc)
- Probe: a synthetic or real traffic exercise that exercises a targeted control path (e.g., prefix cache hit, long context KV replay).
- Fidelity: how much trace/metric detail we collect for a given probe (low/medium/high).
- Rollback trigger: a deterministic rule derived from probe signals (quantile latency, error spike, hallucination-rate from eval set) that causes automatic rollback.

Probe matrix (recommended probes)
1) Cold-start latency probe (low fidelity)
   - Frequency: every 30s for canary clusters; every 5m for standard cluster.
   - Payload: short prompt, multi-token generation to exercise chunking.
   - Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, first-token-time, grpc errors, model-variant used.
   - Use-case: catch kernel regressions and startup regressions.

2) KV-cache rewarm probe (medium fidelity)
   - Frequency: triggered post-deploy and on scale-up events.
   - Payload: long, repeated context that should hit prefix cache. Also alternate with synthetic mismatched prefix to catch cache miss inflation.
   - Traces: include KV cache hit/miss spans (annotate hit reason).
   - Metrics: kv_cache_hit_ratio, kv_cache_eviction_rate, per-request token count.
   - Rollback signal: sustained drop in hit_ratio > 15% and p95 latency regression > 20% for 3 consecutive samples.

3) Batching-pressure probe (low/medium fidelity)
   - Frequency: every 2m with burst variants during business hours.
   - Payloads: mix of 1-token and multi-token requests to simulate realistic batch composition.
   - Metrics: batch_size_distribution, batching_wait_ms, tokens_per_second, queue_length.
   - Traces: capture batch lifecycle spans only when batch_size > threshold to reduce noise.

4) Long-context fidelity probe (high fidelity, limited)
   - Frequency: nighttime or controlled test windows (costly).
   - Payload: long-context generation that stresses KV cache and memory.
   - Collect detailed traces, memory accounting, and kernel selection tags.
   - Use-case: detect regressions in kernel selection or quantization path.

5) ML-quality canary (eval-driven, medium fidelity)
   - Frequency: per-deploy and hourly in early rollout windows.
   - Input: small curated eval set that checks hallucination, repetition, and safety heuristics.
   - Signal: deterioration in answer-quality score vs baseline (A/B comparison).
   - Important: feed into the same rollback decision as latency signals but with independent thresholds (quality-first rollback for obvious regressions).

Sampling and budget rules
- Probe fidelity budget: cap high-fidelity traces to 1% of total trace budget per cluster. Medium fidelity 4%, low fidelity 10%.
- Adaptive sampling: when an alert window opens (latency or error spike), temporarily raise sampling for relevant probe types to high for 15 minutes to gather context.
- Trace size cap: reject or truncate spans above X bytes (configurable) for synthetic probes to prevent bill shock.

Trace annotations and span design (quick rules)
- Always annotate spans with: request_id, tenant_id (if applicable), model_variant, kernel_tag, batch_id, probe_type. Keep tenant_id coarse to avoid PII leakage.
- Design a compact span for fast-latency paths: split into 'dispatch', 'kernel_exec', 'kv_lookup', 'serialize'. Each span should be <= 5 events if possible.
- For high-fidelity probes add a 'probe_assertions' span containing baseline diffs (only for internal probes).

Dashboard notes / templated panels
- Rollout health panel (single row): p50/p95/p99 latency, kv_cache_hit_ratio, batch_wait_ms, synthetic-ml-quality-score. Provide colored thresholds that map to continue/pause/rollback.
- Probe fidelity budget burn rate: rolling window % of trace budget used by probe types.
- Top correlated traces for rolling window: show top 3 trace archetypes that explain latency regressions (dispatch-heavy, kv-heavy, kernel-switch).
- Incident investigation starter: single-click to show recent probe failures, last 10 high-fidelity traces, relevant deploy metadata (git sha, config flags).

Runbook excerpt (automated rollback logic)
- Passive mode (initial 10% traffic canary):
  - If canary p95 latency > baseline p95 * 1.25 for 5 minutes AND kv_cache_hit_ratio drop > 12% -> pause rollout and notify.
  - If ML-quality score drops by >10% on eval set -> immediate pause and human review.
- Aggressive mode (fast rollback):
  - If errors (5xx) spike > 3x baseline for 2 consecutive windows (1m windows) -> automatic rollback to previous model_variant.
- Post-rollback: trigger a focused high-fidelity rewarm probe to validate previous model behaves as expected.

Investigation playbook (SRE/SE)
- Step 1: open Rollout health dashboard, check synthetic probe timeline and last deploy sha.
- Step 2: if p95 regression, pivot to KV-cache rewarm probe traces (look at hit_ratio and eviction spans).
- Step 3: check batching panel; if batch_wait_ms increased and batch_size skewed low, that suggests scheduling regression rather than model kernel issue.
- Step 4: if unclear, escalate to a 15-minute high-sampling window and attach snapshot to incident.

Open questions / TODOs
- Define exact numeric thresholds for ML-quality score per model family (LLama-2 variants vs open weights). Need product/ML input.
- Add a safe-mode probe that injects a small, private-token-limited routing to fallback model for end-to-end verification (privacy concerns need legal approval).
- Instrumentation: do we expose kernel_tag for private deployments? risk of leaking internals to tenants.
- Cost model: run a 2-week experiment with current budget settings to validate probe fidelity percentages.

Notes to self / quick wins
- Add a compact widget showing the last failing probe id and link directly to its high-fidelity trace.
- Implement 'probe-retry' suppression so transient infra flaps don't trigger redundant rollback signals.

References / links
- JIRA: JIRA-OBS-4532 (rollback automation tickets)
- GitHub: telemetry-config PR #78 (probe config schema)
- Slack: #observability (for runbook approvals)

Bottom line
- Probes are the front-line defense for rollout safety. Design them to be targeted, cost-aware, and actionable. Start with the matrix above, run a 2-week tuning window, then lock thresholds into the rollout automation.

Action items (owners)
- Maya: schedule 2-week budget experiment and collect baseline (due 2024-09-17).
- Diego: add probe_id link to dashboard (PR target: telemetry-config #82).
- Priya: draft ML-quality threshold proposal for top 3 model families (due 2024-09-10).
- Jonah: prototype adaptive sampling toggle in agent (prototype branch: feat/adaptive-probes).
